questions.prompt: Your order for 100 shares is partly filled with 60. You send a cancel, and the broker then reports "filled 40". What is the order's final state?
questions.explanation: The other 40 shares traded before the cancel request arrived, so 60 + 40 = 100 are filled. Filled is final, so the cancel has nothing left to remove.

questions.prompt: Why does your program record the state the broker reports instead of setting the state itself when it sends a cancel?
options: A cancel is only a request, and the shares may trade before it arrives
The broker charges a fee each time your program sets a state
Python dataclasses cannot change their fields
Cancels always fail, so there is no point recording them
questions.explanation: Only the broker knows what happened at the market. If you mark the order cancelled yourself and the shares traded, your program believes it holds fewer shares than it does.

questions.prompt: Which states are final, so that no later report can change the order?
questions.explanation: Filled, cancelled and rejected have no entry in the table of allowed moves. An order in one of them is finished.
